strings.d1.s0.name: Stephansdom
strings.d1.s0.tips: Cathedral with a colourful tiled roof; the south tower is 343 steps (6 EUR). Quiet in the morning.
strings.d1.s1.name: Graben & Kohlmarkt
strings.d1.s1.tips: The Plague Column and Demel's shop window; imperial-era streets.
strings.d1.s2.name: Hofburg Sisi Museum
strings.d1.s2.tips: Imperial apartments, the Sisi Museum and the silver collection; audio guide included.
strings.d1.s3.name: Café Central
strings.d1.s3.tips: Vienna coffeehouse with columns; try the Apfelstrudel and a Melange. The queue is about 15 minutes.
strings.d1.s4.name: Wiener Staatsoper
strings.d1.s4.tips: Standing tickets (Stehplatz) go on sale 80 minutes before the show for 13-18 EUR. The opera season runs September to June; closed in summer.
strings.d1.b0.name: Café Sacher Wien
strings.d1.b1.name: Albertina
strings.d1.b1.tips: Dürer's Hare and works from Monet to Picasso; an alternative to the Hofburg.
strings.d2.s0.name: Schönbrunn Palace
strings.d2.s0.tips: The Habsburgs' summer palace; Imperial Tour 22 EUR online, first slot 08:30, includes the Hall of Mirrors.
strings.d2.s1.name: Schönbrunn Gloriette
strings.d2.s1.tips: Walk up the hill through the gardens; coffee at the Gloriette café with a view of the palace.
strings.d2.s2.name: Schönbrunn Zoo
strings.d2.s3.name: Landtmann's Parkcafé Schönbrunn
strings.d2.s3.tips: Café in the palace park; schnitzel and cake.
strings.d2.s4.name: Naschmarkt
strings.d2.s4.tips: A 1.5 km market with Turkish and Balkan stalls, fish at Umar, and a flea market on Saturdays.
strings.d2.b0.name: Neni am Naschmarkt
strings.d2.b0.tips: Tel Aviv cuisine, inside the market.
strings.d2.b1.name: Wagenburg Schönbrunn
strings.d2.b1.tips: Museum of imperial carriages; an alternative to the zoo.
strings.d3.s0.name: Upper Belvedere
strings.d3.s0.tips: Klimt's The Kiss and Schiele; a Baroque palace. Book online.
strings.d3.s1.name: Belvedere Gardens
strings.d3.s1.tips: Gardens between the two palaces; sphinxes.
strings.d3.s2.name: Karlskirche
strings.d3.s2.tips: Baroque dome; take the lift up to the fresco level.
strings.d3.s3.name: Figlmüller Wollzeile
strings.d3.s3.tips: Schnitzel (pork) that spills off the plate, served since 1905. Book ahead; the Bäckerstrasse branch is quieter.
strings.d3.s4.name: Kunsthistorisches Museum
strings.d3.s4.tips: Bruegel collection, Vermeer and a café under the dome; on Maria-Theresien-Platz.
strings.d3.b0.name: Gasthaus Pöschl
strings.d3.b0.tips: Local schnitzel and tafelspitz (boiled beef); a fallback if Figlmüller is full.
strings.d3.b1.name: Secession
strings.d3.b1.tips: Klimt's Beethoven Frieze; the golden cabbage dome.
strings.d4.s0.name: Wiener Riesenrad
strings.d4.s0.tips: Ferris wheel from 1897; the setting of The Third Man. No queue in the morning.
strings.d4.s1.name: Prater Hauptallee
strings.d4.s1.tips: A 4 km chestnut-lined avenue; cycling and the Lusthaus.
strings.d4.s2.name: Schweizerhaus Prater
strings.d4.s2.tips: Closed in winter; go to Prater Alm or the Lusthaus instead.
strings.d4.s3.name: Donauinsel
strings.d4.s4.name: Hundertwasserhaus
strings.d4.s4.tips: Colourful apartment block with wavy floors; seen from outside. The Kunst Haus Wien museum is nearby.
strings.d4.b0.name: Lusthaus Prater
strings.d4.b0.tips: Historic pavilion restaurant at the end of the park.
strings.d4.b1.name: Alte Donau Boat
strings.d4.b1.tips: Pedal boat on the Old Danube; an alternative to the island.
strings.d5.s0.name: Melk Abbey
strings.d5.s0.tips: 1 hour by train; Baroque abbey and library with Danube views. Use the ÖBB Wachau combination ticket (train, boat and abbey).
strings.d5.s1.name: Melk-Krems Danube Boat
strings.d5.s1.tips: 2 hours along the valley; vineyards and castles (Dürnstein).
strings.d5.s2.name: Dürnstein
strings.d5.s2.tips: Town with a blue tower; climb to the castle where Richard the Lionheart was held.
strings.d5.s3.name: Dürnstein Heuriger
strings.d5.s3.tips: Grüner Veltliner and apricot products at a wine tavern; Wachau apricots.
strings.d5.s4.name: Krems Steiner Tor
strings.d5.s4.tips: The old town gate of Krems; return train at 17:00.
strings.d5.b0.name: Loibnerhof Unterloiben
strings.d5.b0.tips: Famous Wachau restaurant, next to Dürnstein.
strings.d5.b1.name: Weissenkirchen
strings.d5.b1.tips: Wine village; stop here by boat instead of Krems.
strings.d6.s0.name: MuseumsQuartier
strings.d6.s0.tips: Leopold Museum (Schiele) and the courtyard seating; mumok.
strings.d6.s1.name: Spittelberg
strings.d6.s1.tips: Biedermeier streets; Christmas market in December.
strings.d6.s2.name: Glacis Beisl Spittelberg
strings.d6.s2.tips: Beisl (Viennese tavern) with a garden behind the MQ; Viennese home cooking.
strings.d6.s3.name: Grinzing Heuriger Mayer am Pfarrplatz
strings.d6.s3.tips: Wine tavern in Beethoven's former home; take bus 38A. Try the Sturm (September) and Liptauer.
strings.d6.s4.name: Kahlenberg
strings.d6.s4.tips: City and Danube views from the top of the Vienna Woods; take the 38A, go at sunset.
strings.d6.b0.name: Heuriger Sirbu
strings.d6.b0.tips: Wine tavern with views among the Nussberg vineyards; May to October.
strings.d6.b1.name: Karl-Marx-Hof
strings.d6.b1.tips: Red Vienna's 1 km-long housing block; Heiligenstadt.
strings.d7.s0.name: Café Sperl
strings.d7.s0.tips: Coffeehouse from 1880; billiard tables and newspapers, ideal for a farewell breakfast.
strings.d7.s1.name: Mariahilfer Strasse
strings.d7.s2.name: Imperial Treasury Vienna
strings.d7.s2.tips: The Habsburg crown and the Holy Lance; Hofburg.
strings.d7.s3.name: Wien Hauptbahnhof CAT
strings.d7.s3.tips: City Airport Train takes 16 minutes (or S7, 30 minutes); farewell.
strings.d7.b0.name: Demel
strings.d7.b0.tips: The Hofburg's pastry shop; Sacher's rival.
strings.d7.b1.name: Haus der Musik
strings.d7.b1.tips: Sound museum; conduct the Philharmonic virtually.
strings.note0: Wiener Linien 24-hour pass 10 EUR, 7-day pass about 25 EUR (48/72-hour passes discontinued); CAT or S7 to the airport. The city is walkable; take a tram for a Ring tour or two.
strings.note1: Schönbrunn and Belvedere have timed online tickets; opera standing tickets are sold at the box office 80 minutes before (opera closed in summer).
strings.note2: Christmas markets in November and December (Rathaus, Schönbrunn, Spittelberg) and ball season in January and February; winter is 0-5°C and coffeehouses are at their best.
strings.note3: Schnitzel 20-25 EUR (Figlmüller); in a coffeehouse a Melange is 5 EUR and cake 6 EUR; Sturm at a heuriger in autumn. Tip 5-10%.
strings.note4: Shops are closed on Sundays; museums are open.
strings.note5: For the Wachau, use the ÖBB combination ticket; apricot blossom in April, wine harvest in September and October.
